statement: Assume the Program 2 target-span-two reductions and suppose a primitive coprime leading pencil contains a fourth power, normalized as H4=(x^4,Q,0) with x not dividing Q. The highest Keller equation routes the cubic and, when necessary, quadratic normal layers to an aligned pure-power, binary, or quadratic-source branch; under the recorded Program 2 inputs every resulting branch is automorphic or already excluded.
title: The Primitive Fourth-Power Locus Adds No Quartic Counterexample Leaf
